assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is the clearest case of a general method that changed how chemists build bonds: arylamines are now made routinely in academia and in pharmaceutical process chemistry, and ligand design made a hard transformation routine. The adoption record is visible in countless syntheses and industrial routes. Its chemical novelty is unquestionable, and it complements the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, broadly general versions in parallel and independently from the mid-1990s, with ligand generations from both groups. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling was a precursor but not the general catalytic method; I would not include him, though I cannot independently verify the full priority history.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of confirmation, with industrial use at scale; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit Kosugi (and possibly Migita) for the precursor tin-amide chemistry.
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be read as incremental by some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes synthetic logic by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional groups, shortening routes to complex molecules and enabling late-stage modification in drug discovery. Directing-group, ligand-accelerated and Pd(II)/Pd(IV) approaches opened a large field that is widely used.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand- and template-controlled, meta/remote and enantioselective C-H activation) and Sanford (Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis and late-stage functionalization) are the most decisive; Hartwig, Daugulis and Smith also made key contributions (borylation, directing-group arylation), so the allocation is genuinely contested and I leave Hartwig out only to keep the trio clean and avoid duplicating B004.
assessment.maturity: Strong, broad uptake, but the field is still evolving and the most general, predictable methods are arguably not yet fully mature; timing is plausible rather than clearly overdue.
uncertainties: Credit is spread across many groups and several distinct mechanistic strategies.
Whether the field is a single discovery or a collection of methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry is the chemical basis of automated oligonucleotide synthesis, underpinning PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a textbook example of a reliable, efficient synthetic method that became routine and indispensable.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite coupling chemistry (with Beaucage); Hood is credited here mainly for automation and instrumentation, which I regard as secondary to the chemical invention. I propose Caruthers alone, noting Beaucage is not in the credited names and I cannot add him.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of continuous, universal use; very mature and, if anything, long delayed.
uncertainties: Credit of Beaucage and others is not representable in this list.
Possible reservation that the prize logic leans on enabling tools rather than a new conceptual advance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were difficult before, and is now commonplace in medicinal chemistry and process settings. The chemical novelty is real, even if building on earlier photochemistry.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational synthetic photoredox papers around 2008-2009, while Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre made important parallel or earlier contributions. Attribution is messy, and MacMillan's 2021 prize may weigh against a second award.
assessment.maturity: Rapid, wide adoption over about 15 years; stable, but a prize may still be somewhat early relative to the leading methods above.
uncertainties: MacMillan is already a laureate (2021, organocatalysis).
Early photochemical precedents and multi-group priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes changed the understanding of bonding and gave N-heterocyclic carbenes as ligands and organocatalysts, central to modern metathesis catalysts, cross-coupling ligands and organocatalysis. The concept turned a presumed laboratory curiosity into a general tool.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand isolated the first stable carbene (phosphino-silyl carbene, 1988) and Arduengo the first crystalline NHC (1991); both are decisive. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are important for applications rather than the discovery itself.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with decades of use; maturity is high.
uncertainties: Weight between the fundamental isolation and the later catalytic applications.
The 2005 and 2010 prizes already credit NHC-based catalysts downstream.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows the chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical. It is a clean, general chemical idea with wide use in protein science and therapeutics research.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported NCL in 1994, and Muir (expressed protein ligation) extended it to semisynthesis; Danishefsky and others contributed to later developments. A Kent-Dawson-Muir configuration looks defensible.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use and confirmation; mature, though the field is somewhat specialized.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact relative to the top-ranked methods.
Distribution of credit with Danishefsky, Liu and Brik.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that main-group combinations can activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, a conceptually new reactivity principle with applications in metal-free hydrogenation.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported reversible H2 activation by a phosphine-borane in 2006; Erker contributed major early mechanistic and scope work. The two-person attribution is clean.
assessment.maturity: Concept well confirmed, but practical impact on routine synthesis is still limited; possibly premature compared with higher-ranked methods.
uncertainties: Limited industrial or broad synthetic adoption so far.
Relative novelty versus earlier main-group work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization provided controlled radical polymerization of many monomers with defined architectures, a general method widely used in materials synthesis and industry.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto (with Kamigaito) independently reported metal-catalyzed living radical polymerization in 1995; Wang is a coauthor with Matyjaszewski. I credit Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto-Kamigaito, while overlap with RAFT (B035) complicates how polymer control is recognized.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use; mature, though the committee may prefer polymer chemistry recognition in a different configuration.
uncertainties: Competing recognition of RAFT and nitroxide-mediated routes.
Polymer chemistry has had few recent prizes, so field balance is unclear.
